key_insight: Block-triangular joint drifting turns single-step trajectory data into a one-step generative surrogate by preserving the current-state marginal while directly sampling the next-state conditional distribution.
engineering_relevance: This enables fast stochastic simulation with one model evaluation per time step, making it attractive for uncertainty-aware scientific computing and reduced-cost trajectory generation.
method: Apply a projected drift field to the joint distribution of consecutive states rather than to next-state conditionals alone.
Use a block-triangular architecture so the first block preserves the current-state marginal and the second block generates the next-state sample.
Avoid auxiliary generative substeps between time steps, yielding a direct one-step surrogate.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments showing accurate marginal and trajectory-dependent statistics and favorable accuracy-cost tradeoffs versus deterministic, diffusion-, flow-, and distillation-based surrogates.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and representativeness of standard trajectory data, which provide only one realized next state per current state and may limit learning in sparse or highly multimodal regimes.
paper_title: One-Step Generative Surrogate Models via Block-Triangular Joint Drifting
